submission.justification: Simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c (100k events each): R1 peaks at about 4.77 sigma at 3 cm (6 cm: 3.34 sigma); R2 gives 3.97 sigma at 3 cm (2 cm: 3.70, 6 cm: 2.94); R3 gives 2.10 sigma at 6 cm. R1 has the best separation, but it is a high-index porous radiator with no humidity treatment, and no project document contains the humidity-ageing transparency data needed to show it stays within the 10% hard limit. R2 is the porous radiator with a hydrophobic treatment, which is the relevant mitigation for humidity ageing. I recommend R2 at 3 cm as the best separation among candidates whose humidity resistance is plausibly adequate. However, its 10% transparency-loss compliance is not verified: no ageing data exists in the documents and the simulation tool does not report transparency. Compliance must be confirmed with a 10-year humidity ageing test before procurement. If R2 fails that test, R3 is the only remaining fallback, and its separation is much lower (about 2.1 sigma at 6 cm). R1 should only be chosen if its ageing test shows less than 10% transparency loss, since it would then give about 1.2 sigma more separation. Thickness of 3 cm was the best tested for R2; 4 and 5 cm were not scanned.
